answer: Sybil resistance makes coordinated equivocation costly: when k identities forge conflicting attestations, correlated penalties grow as O(k²), rather than as k independent fines. Detection also triggers an exponential multiplier in capital loss across the bonded escrows, so adding identities amplifies exposure instead of diluting it. The trellis of shared evidence reveals coordination, while asymmetric depreciation ensures a rising tide of detected offenses rapidly erodes recoverable stake.
